evidence.baseline: The Greatest Untapped Resource ... The greatest untapped resource on this planet is not under any seabed or in any mineral seam. It is human potential.
evidence.shipped: Human Capacity Is Not a Resource Deposit ... Human capacity is not a mineral reserve.

findings.authorizedBy: Not authorized by any catalog category or ledger item. This is a substitution that reverses the section.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline uses the extractive vocabulary deliberately and turns it: every other resource is finite and depleting, this one is generative and inexhaustible. That turn is the argument, and it is a good one. The pass read the metaphor as a defect, deleted the turn, and left a rebuttal of a passage that no longer exists. Seventy percent of the words went with it.

findings.summary: The contrast between depleting and generative resources was cut.

evidence.baseline: Every other resource we have learned to extract is finite and depleting; this one is generative and, so far as we can tell, inexhaustible, and almost wholly unworked.

findings.diagnosis: So far as we can tell is the volume hedging its own strongest claim, which is exactly the honesty the corpus card asks for, and almost wholly unworked is the sentence that makes the section urgent rather than merely appreciative.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Two em dashes. One introduced an appositive enumeration and became a comma. One added a final clause and became a comma within a rebuilt sentence.
The seabed and mineral seam refusal, human potential and its four capacities, the finite and generative contrast, and the closing definition of the praxis.
The prior pass objection to the metaphor, rewritten as the volume acknowledging the risk in its own word rather than as a correction of a passage that is no longer there.

openQuestions.question: Heading not changed. Baseline: The Greatest Untapped Resource. Current: Human Capacity Is Not a Resource Deposit. The current heading states the rebuttal rather than the section, so a reader meets a correction before meeting the claim it corrects. The prose now carries both. Changing the heading back would retire a public route and is not an editorial decision.

The restored section calls human potential a resource and says it is inexhaustible. The prior pass judged that this repeats the extractive logic the volume opposes. The re-render restores the passage and states the risk. This is a tone and claim scope decision that belongs to the author.

evidence.baseline: The greatest untapped resource on this planet is not under any seabed or in any mineral seam. It is human potential
evidence.shipped: We use the word resource here against its own grain, and the risk in it should be said plainly. A capacity described as a deposit invites the very logic this volume opposes. Nothing here licenses the mining of a person.

improvements.note: The baseline borrows extraction's own vocabulary to praise what it says must not be extracted and never notices the borrowing. The kept paragraph notices, in the volume's voice, and the current heading makes the same correction structurally. Promoted from a quiet kept to a credited finding.
